payload.title: Stacked board layout on phones in @kanbus/ui
payload.description:
Driver: the horizontal board is a poor experience on phones in the Papyrus newsroom CMS. Below a viewport width breakpoint the board becomes one vertical column, with each status column as a section. This belongs in @kanbus/ui so every host (Papyrus, Chatticus, the Kanbus console) gets it through Board and IssueCollection.

Design decisions:
- API: layout?: 'auto' | 'columns' | 'stacked' on Board and IssueCollection, default 'auto', plus stackedBelowWidth?: number, default 768. Stacked applies below 768 px, so tablets in portrait (768 and up) keep columns.
- Viewport, not container: opening a detail panel narrows the board, and that must not flip the layout and lose the reader's place. A host that embeds the board in a narrow side panel passes layout='stacked' explicitly.
- One scroller: stacked mode has one vertical scroller and one virtualizer over a flat list of section headers and cards, so a 500-card column stays bounded. Stacking the existing per-column virtualizers would nest scrollers on a phone.
- Same state and selectors: collapsed columns share the existing state and storage key, config-collapsed statuses stay collapsed, and .kb-column-header, .issue-card and aria-expanded keep working for hosts and tests.

Tasks run in order: stacked layout core, near-end callback, themes and touch, console, release. The Papyrus newsroom rollout is tracked on the PPY board and depends on the release.
